input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which satisfies the first preferred element. However, the Agreement contains no forum or venue provision anywhere: searches for court, jurisdiction, venue, arbitration and dispute resolution return nothing, and the remaining general provisions (10.1-10.8) address only notices, joint venture, assignment, waiver, severability, survival, entire agreement and headings. Without an exclusive forum, disputes on the merits could be litigated in any jurisdiction, so the clause fails the fallback forum element as well. We added a single sentence fixing exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, with a carve-out only for temporary injunctive relief, leaving the existing choice-of-law wording untouched.

ops.text: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.5 already applies New York law, but the Agreement has no forum clause. proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County venue to the New York governing law clause.
